evidence: StockAllocationService.reserve collects StockShortage entries from product.canReserve and throws InsufficientStockError before reserving anything. This is the all-or-nothing reservation rule, which is domain logic.
release and commit hand the work to the Product entity methods (product.release, product.commit), which is domain behaviour.
productFor reads from an in-memory ReadonlyMap that the caller supplies. It does not fetch from a repository or database.
The file has no framework decorators, HTTP, ORM or I/O code. Its only imports are domain entities, value objects and errors.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain/services/StockAllocationService.ts is a pure domain service. It defines the StockAllocator domain interface and an implementation that applies the stock-reservation rule. The reserve method checks every line first, collects shortages, throws InsufficientStockError, and only then reserves, so a reservation happens for all lines or none. The release and commit methods hand the work to the Product entity methods. The file has no persistence, transport, framework, DI decorators, I/O or orchestration logic. It works only on in-memory entities supplied through ProductLookup and raises domain errors. Every responsibility fits the domain layer.
